task.outcome_horizon: 6 years from the initial PROJECT_START (typical R01 project periods are 3-5 years, so the first competing renewal normally begins in year 4-6); cohorts through FY2017 are fully observed using files through FY2023.
task.population: Extramural R01 awards in the annual NIH ExPORTER project files with APPLICATION_TYPE code 1 (new), SUPPORT_YEAR code 1, ACTIVITY code R01, non-missing PROJECT_START, AWARD_NOTICE_DATE and ORG_STATE, and AWARD_NOTICE_DATE from 2007-10-01 through 2017-09-30 (federal fiscal years 2008-2017). The released splits ship fiscal years 2008-2012 to train, 2013-2014 to eval, and 2015-2016 to holdout; the FY2017 cohort is held back outside the three release files as a post-holdout drift audit. Excludes other application types, contracts with N-prefix codes, intramural Z-prefix codes, and projects whose first-year record is missing. Eligibility uses only fields visible on the award record at the decision instant.
task.prediction_time: The award notice date (AWARD_NOTICE_DATE) printed on the project first-year record, the moment the new award becomes public. Features use only fields printed on that first-year record or histories built from R01 award records with AWARD_NOTICE_DATE strictly earlier than the row notice date.
task.question: When NIH announces a brand-new R01 award, will that project later be continued through a competing-renewal award on the same core project number, or will the project end without one?
task.simple_references: Persistence/majority baseline: each fiscal-year cohort renewal rate, constant per split. Calendar baseline: fiscal-year cohort and project start month. Identity baseline: organization identifier ORG_IPF_CODE and administering institute/review panel. No persistence score column exists in the source; the identity reference uses only shipped entity columns and training-only calendar rates.
task.split_policy: One row per new award; assignment by AWARD_NOTICE_DATE with hard fiscal-year boundaries (Oct 1 - Sep 30) and no shuffling: train FY2008-FY2012, eval FY2013-FY2014, holdout FY2015-FY2016; FY2017 is held back as a post-holdout drift check and never used for tuning. No calendar embargo gap is imposed, because every feature for a row is restricted to records dated strictly before that row's notice date, and every label uses only post-decision records of that same core project; instead right-censoring is enforced by requiring the full 6-year window to be observed at the data cutoff. Identity/aggregate features additionally obey the rule that they may use only cohorts whose outcome window closed before the decision instant, so a later row can never disclose an earlier row's target.
task.target: y = 1 if the same CORE_PROJECT_NUM has any award record with APPLICATION_TYPE = 2 (competing continuation / competing renewal) whose BUDGET_START is strictly after the initial PROJECT_START and no later than initial PROJECT_START + 6 years; y = 0 if no such record exists and the cohort's full 6-year window is observed in the data cutoff. Rows whose window is not fully observed are dropped, never labeled 0.
task.usefulness: The binary outcome is not stored in any field: it requires reconstructing project continuity across annual support-year records and award types. It is uncommon rather than balanced: in the previously constructed FY2008-FY2017 release roughly 4,300 of 39,875 first-year R01 rows (about one in nine) received a competing renewal inside six years, so a constant negative baseline already reaches about 89 percent accuracy and the signal must be read from ranking and calibration metrics. The outcome still varies across institutes, review panels, organizations and investigator experience, so a model must beat fiscal-year cohort base rates and institutional identity baselines using only award-time metadata, and it must avoid the documented contamination channel in which PROJECT_END is extended on renewal.

cross_row_audit.auxiliary_files_review: Only the declared train, eval and holdout CSV files are written; no auxiliary evaluation or answer files.
cross_row_audit.rationale: The task is an event-level tabular release with one row per first-year R01 award; identity clustering is handled by evaluation rather than by extra files.

limitations: Retrospective snapshot, not a historical operational feed: each annual file reflects the administrative state of records when that file was created, so later revisions, amount changes, no-cost extensions and PI moves appear in the downloaded vintage.
Historical first-year availability of each field is assumed from the current publisher data dictionary and annual files, not verified against an archived vintage.
Actual ExPORTER publication timestamps are not established, so timing.observations is empty rather than filled with invented dates.
PROJECT_END is excluded from features because NIH extends it on renewal; using it would leak the outcome.

The outcome is partly behavioral: a renewal exists only if the investigator applied, so the label measures continuation of federal funding rather than scientific merit alone and co-moves with appropriations and institute paylines.
Rows are not independent draws: prolific investigators and large institutions contribute many rows, so cluster-aware evaluation by organization and investigator history is advisable.
PI identifier values are not perfectly stable over time, so PI histories carry linkage noise.

Cost amounts: NIH's data dictionary describes direct and indirect cost amounts as available only for awards funded in FY2012 onward, but the current-vintage annual files used here populate the pre-FY2012 population cohorts as well (measured in the last release: no blank direct amounts and only a handful of blank indirect amounts across released rows). The descriptor now follows the measured vintage; blanks still remain missing rather than zero.
Prior R01 history is left-censored before the first downloaded annual file, so early-cohort prior-count features may undercount older awards.

The solicitation identifier (OPPORTUNITY_NUMBER, the FOA number) is exposed in every audited annual ExPORTER project file, but it is not shipped: the frozen feature contract for this task is the twelve award-time metadata columns, so omitting the solicitation identifier is a declared scope decision rather than a claim that the publisher files lack the column.
No label-derived PI or organization renewal-rate feature is shipped; this is a completed check, not an unresolved item.
The legal basis is U.S. law and territorial: 17 U.S.C. 105 removes U.S. copyright in these agency-compiled records; it is not a worldwide dedication.
Grantee-supplied text such as abstracts, titles and public health relevance statements is excluded from features and release.

The discovery-time provenance strings in the frozen source block (its limitations list, its construction.source_examples note and its reason summary) are preserved verbatim from source discovery and are not the operative evaluation descriptor. Two of those sentences describe an earlier snapshot: the claim that direct and indirect cost amounts are blank before FY2012 is superseded by the measured current-vintage statement above, and the phrase describing a roughly balanced label is superseded by the measured roughly eleven percent positive rate. PI identifiers are used only to derive counts and are never shipped. No built row or feature depends on those provenance sentences.
